title: Celeriac and Parsnip Purée with Crisp Parsnip Ribbons
summary: Celeriac, parsnips and garlic softened in butter, braised covered with stock and herbs until falling apart, then blended silky with warm milk. Finished with fried parsnip ribbons.

ingredients.item: celeriac, peeled and cut into 2.5 cm cubes
parsnips, peeled and sliced 1 cm thick
fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Soften
steps.text: Melt the butter in the large pan over medium heat. Add the celeriac, parsnips and garlic and cook for 10-12 min, stirring now and then, until softened and lightly coloured.

steps.title: Braise
steps.text: Add the stock, thyme, bay and salt, cover and cook on low for 30-40 min, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables crush easily. Uncover for 2 min to let the steam escape and remove the herbs.

steps.title: Fry the ribbons
steps.text: Meanwhile, peel the small parsnip into long ribbons. Heat 2-3 cm oil in the small pan to 170 °C and fry the ribbons in small batches for about 1 min until golden. Drain on the tray.

steps.title: Blend and serve
steps.text: Blend the vegetables with the warm milk for 2 min until silky, scraping down the sides. Season with pepper, swoosh onto warm plates and top with the crisp ribbons.

tips: Blend while hot for the smoothest result.
For a richer purée, swap the milk for single cream.
It pairs well with roast meats and seared fish.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Refrigerate the purée up to 3 days and reheat until piping hot (74 °C) with a splash of milk. Fry the ribbons fresh. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
